If I'm to be completely honest the games fairly mediocre most of the time. I don't care for the voiced protagonist one bit, not because its broken Bethesdas usual trend of voice less player character but because the conversation options don't give any indication of the actual dialogue your character will say and your options are incredibly narrow. Bethesda really shot themselves in the foot with this one imho because the conversations went from being an interesting aspect of Fallout3 and NV to fairly tedious neutral and generic replies to randomly out of context emotional replies, at one point my character went from angry to whimsically sarcastic because I accidentally hit the wrong key when I wanted to steer the conversation a particular way and it had absolutely no effect on the situation because it looped right back around to the same set of options until I picked the one "progress" option available.

Most conversations break down into one or two options laid out as though you've got more options than you really do,

--- ---
Yes I'll do what you asked -
Yes I'll do what you asked for some money -
I want to know more before I say Yes -
Yes but I'll try to say it sarcastically -
No I won't do what you asked yet -

There's no real motivation to interact with any of the factions other than to move some parts of the main quest along and while some NPC's and companions are quite colorful and interesting at first it gets really bland really quickly because as I said earlier your forced to role play as Bethesda has intended so you can't be a particular kind of character other than what Bethesda recorded lines for. Pro tip: don't bother doing too many Minutemen quests (don't take the castle) and don't try to create too many settlements, the only perk for doing these quests is to give you a shared inventory across the wasteland, if I bother doing a second play though I won't be creating any settlements.

I have to say the game doesn't look that much better from Skyrim with the Bethesda HD texture pack and performance is absolutely shit near any of the urban areas like Diamond City, Goodneighbor and Boston city in general. I've tried running the game at the lowest settings and resolution possible and in certain areas the FPS will always drop to the low 30s. Most of the time my 280x.will happily keep a solid 60fps but certain areas that have a lot of godrays and shadows just kills the immersion. Whats probably the worst thing about the performance is the fact that the game does not scale to lesser hardware, laptop users and anyone on running lowered tier hardware from 4~5 year old might want to give the game a miss until its had a few optimization patches and the performance improvement mods mature a lot more.

Now those are the biggest areas that the game fails to deliver on but what it does do really well is the incredibly detailed world you're given to explore and the combat feels a lot better than Bethesda's other open world RPGs. You'll curse like a salty sailor when RNG bullets miss a ghoul 6 feet away from you and you might regret picking any perks that effect VATS early on because iron sighting is infinitely more accurate but eventually as you take the right combat perks and start finding or upgrading to better weapons it becomes less of a issue. It brings me onto another point, the new streamlined perk system isn't bad but most of it outside of the damage increases doesn't feel useful, there is almost no point in putting any effort into building up charisma unless you absolutely have to have a perk that requires a base charisma.

The settlement building mechanics are pretty tedious at times, you'll run out of junk / materials too often or find that you can't really make any buildings that are as complex as you'd like. I'm not sure why its in the game and if I had to guess its heavily inspired by survival games like Rust and Arc but its no where near as robust and doesn't really fit into the whole exploration driven gameplay that makes Bethesda games what they are. That said I wouldn't call this a negative aspect of the game, its almost if not completely option and if its something you like then you might enjoy it for a while, personally I could take it or leave it.

I'll finish by saying this, its not Fallout3, NV, Oblivion or Skyrim tier good but its still pretty good fun just don't expect the same kind of RPG experience. Its good but its as though Bethesda focus grouped the design a bit too much trying to be an action shooter / survival builder instead of a RPG.

I'm not a fan, the only thing of significance that was improved was the shooting. Sure there were some other minor improvements like weapon modding (though unfortunately that system is a whole heap of missed opportunities, most upgrades seem to be a stat increase with only a few that add actually meaningful features to the weapon, doesn't feel any more developed than NV weapon mods) and the town building which while initially interesting it quickly began to feel tacked on and I stopped giving a damn about my settlements, not to mention the controls feel quite clunky and I often had issues getting the objects to align properly despite them sometimes snapping together just fine. I also really don't like the removal of skills, or simplification of SPECIAL. The perk tree without skills reminded me of RPG elements added to a Action game instead of a true RPG. all RIP in peace factions and reputation.

As for bugs I've run into quite a few but that par for the course of a Bethesda game, my bugs were primarily non game breaking (only 3 CTDs in about 20 hours and one save that wont load) although I have a few quests I couldn't complete without console commands do to NPCs disappearing or getting stuck in walls, primarily I've been getting more annoyances than fatal errors things like physics breaking, textures not loading in, randomly teleporting during VATS and the similar, most were fixable by saving and reloading and/or restarting the game. I guess it's a bit more stable than FO3 and FNV were on launch.

I can forgive bugs (after all NV is one of my favorite games of all time and it had a really broken release due to obsidian being forced to release it early), I can forgive the graphics being a little behind the curve or the animations having that patented Bethesda stiffness to them, these things can and will be fixed by the modding community (though that doesn't completely absolve Bethesda). And if those were the only issues with the game then I'd still like it (would still be my least favorite of the new Bethesda style fallout, but I'd probably still play it for a hundred hours) but the nail in the coffin is the dialogue, dear dog the voiced protagonist ruins everything. In the vast majority of cases the dialogue options break down to: yes, sarcastic yes, tell me more about why I need to say yes, and yes latter. I felt like Yes Man was uploading into a synth body and that is the MC. It pretty much kills RP, and it's goddamn disgusting that The Witcher 3 a game with a fixed protagonist who has a preexisting personality and code of morals has similar or more options on how to handle a situation than Fallout, a series known for player choice.

The power armor is pretty cool though I didn't like how early it was handed to you.

I really wanted to like Fallout 4, I really did, Even after I initially quit the game 12 hours in I came back for a second attempt just to see if I was missing something. It feels like it took 1 step forward 3 steps back. Maybe it's just because I was hoping for a Fallout game and instead got a FPS with RPGlite mechanics in the Fallout universe.
